_comment: An ally's join condition as a situation of its own (Expansion 6 F.1, docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.6: bury a parent, be persuaded): a tale's recruit step met in its person's town may become one of these (story/situations.for_step; the beast's hunter has its own, situations.inside.json). Their endings give the tale its key 'ally' (game/story/stakes.join then brings them in); a lapse finishes the step without them, so the tale is never stuck. Words as in situations.inside.json, with the tale's own.

note: {asker}'s father died the week the graves opened, and lies in the cold-house still: the priest will not bury anyone in that ground until the dead stop walking out of it.
{asker} will not leave until the old man is in the ground, properly, with the words said, and nobody in {town} will dig a grave this month.
{asker}'s mother lies wrapped in the barn, unburied, because the sexton fled when the dead walked. {asker} will not go anywhere while she lies there.

label: I know the words. We bury them tonight, you and I, and I will say them.
say: ...You'd do that? Then get a spade. We'll do it right.
Tonight, then. I'll fetch the lantern.
fail_say: You don't know them. Not the old ones, not the right ones. I'll not have it done wrong.

label: The priest will bury them if the price is right. I'll pay it.
say: ...They'll do it for that, aye. They'd do anything for that. Thank you.

label: Not the old ground, then. The hill above {town}, and I'll talk the reeve into it.
say: The reeve gives way. It takes you and {asker} half the night to dig, in ground like iron, but it is done, and a stone is on it.
Leave is given, grudgingly. Blisters, a broken spade, and a grave on the hill at dawn: it is done.
fail_say: The reeve will not hear of a grave outside the churchyard, and {asker} sends you away.

line: You buried them together, and {asker} stood a long time at the grave, and then turned to you: "Now. Where do we go?"
The grave is on the hill, and the words were said. {asker} owes you that, and means to pay it standing beside you.
{asker} will never forget who held the lantern while the grave was dug. When you go, {asker} goes.
They are buried at last, and {asker} is free to come with you.
The priest said the words, for a price, and {asker} wept, and then went for {asker_their} spear.
It is done properly. {asker} will stand with you now.
{asker} buried them alone, in the end, and will not leave {town} now. Not for you.
Too late: {asker} has dug the grave alone and sat by it since, and has no strength left for anything else.
{asker} stayed to bury them, and stayed after. You go on without {asker_them}.

title: The unburied
A grave to dig
{asker}'s dead
stakes: whether {asker} can leave the dead unburied to fight the dead
a burial no one in {town} will do
plea: I'll come. I want to come. But not while they lie there with no grave. I can't. You understand that. You must.
They're in the cold-house, wrapped in a sheet, and the priest won't touch them. How can I go, with that?
Bury them first. That's all I ask. Bury them right, and I'll follow you into the barrow itself.
first: {asker} will stand with you, once a grave is dug that nobody in {town} will dig.
{asker} has a parent to bury, and the ground is the ground the dead are walking out of.
The one who might stand with you is {asker}, who cannot leave the dead unburied.
ask: They say you're the one who'd stand with us.
Will you come, when we go up there?
I need a spear beside me at the barrow.
take: I'll see them in the ground. Then you come.
thanks: Then I'll be waiting, with a spade.

note: {asker} has seen heroes come through {town} before, and bury no one but the folk who followed them.
{asker} went with the last band that rode out to fight something, and was the only one who came back.
{asker} does not believe the dead can be fought, and says so to anyone who will listen.

label: Who were they, the last ones who asked you?
say: ...Three of them, in good mail, with a banner. They wanted a guide. I guided them. I came back.
Hired swords, the last ones. They talked like you. They're still up there.

label: I am not them. Here is what I have done, and why I will win.
say: ...You're not them. No. Maybe not. All right. I'll come.
I'll believe it when I see it. But I'll come and see it.
fail_say: They said all that too. Every word of it.

label: You came back because you ran. There is no shame in it. Tell me the rest.
say: {asker} is quiet a long time. Then it all comes out, the whole of it, and when it is done {asker} looks lighter. "All right. All right. I'll come, and I'll not run this time."
fail_say: "You know nothing about it," {asker} says, and turns away.

line: {asker} told you the worst of it, and you did not look away. When you go, {asker} goes.
Said aloud at last: {asker} ran, once, and means to stand this time, beside you.
"Nobody ever asked me that," {asker} says. "They all just called me lucky." {asker} will come.
{asker} still has doubts, and will come anyway.
Persuaded, if not convinced: {asker} will stand with you.
{asker} has decided to believe you. It cost {asker_them} something to decide it.
{asker} made up {asker_their} mind in the end, and the answer is no.
You waited too long to answer {asker}, and {asker} took the silence for an answer.
{asker} will wait and see how it goes for you. From a safe distance.

title: The doubter
Why {asker} will not follow
One who came back
stakes: the one in {town} who has been up there and lived
plea: I've followed people like you before. I came back and they didn't. Why would I do it again?
You want me up there with you. Everyone does. Give me a reason, a real one.
Tell me why you're different. Go on. I've heard it all.
first: {asker} could stand with you, and does not believe you can win.
{asker} came back from the last band that went up there, alone.
The one who might stand with you is {asker}, who has followed heroes before.
ask: They say you're the one who knows the way up there.
I hear you've been up there.
